newsitem.title: USA: Cash crude barrel prices ease slightly in US Gulf.
newsitem.headline: Cash crude barrel prices ease slightly in US Gulf.

text.p: Cash crude barrels in the U.S. Gulf attracted steady to slightly weaker prices Friday morning as the threat of extended Colombian production delays and hurricane damage to oil facilities eased, traders said.
August West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was around 10-15 cents weaker at $19.80-90 a barrel, and held a nine cent discount to the September benchmark.

Hurricane Danny was last reported drifting along the U.S. Gulf Coast, with no reports of damage to oil platforms or refineries in the region. Chevron, however, said it was shutting its 295,000 barrels per day refinery in Pascagoula, Mississippi as a precaution. No other major refineries were reported shut.
Cash dealers said Chevron would likely be able to "ramp" up production once the storm threat abates, causing no major supply crisis.
"From the look of the storm, it looks like Pascagoula would be the only refinery in the way," said a Gulf trader.

Occidental Petroleum Corp said it resumed pumping along the Cano Limon-Covenas pipeline in Colombia after repairs were completed earlier Friday. The line was closed for the better part of two weeks after leftist rebels dynamited the structure, forcing Occidental and state oil company Ecopetrol to declare force majeure on cargoes and Cano output.

For the grades, the end of the week brought about deals in most categories, led by Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James selling at 25 cents over August WTI/Cushing, down from premiums of more than 30 cents on Wednesday. Since Hurricane Danny has passed thus far without seriously impacting the oil refinery and production belt, LLS prices have eased back, traders said.
Other deals saw Midland/WTI sell at 22 cents under WTI/Cushing and Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire 25 cents cheaper than the August WTI/Cushing.
WTI/Cushing Postings Plus sold at $1.98, working off the wider August/September roll.
